set.body:
calculate_effective_df() (R/effective_df.R:47-57) computes the AR df adjustment as

  denom <- 1 + 2 * sum(1 - k/n)

which is the variance-inflation factor you would get if EVERY autocorrelation were
exactly 1.0. It never receives phi. .fast_t_contrast calls it at R/con_stats.R:544
whenever ar_order > 0, feeding pval <- 2*pt(-abs(tval), df_effective) at :550 - so
it governs the mainline AR path, not a dormant corner.

Measured, n=200 p=12 AR(1): the live formula returns 62.9 df for every phi, where a
phi-aware adjustment spans 170.2 (phi=0.05) to 10.4 (phi=0.9). It is also applied to
data that has ALREADY been whitened, so it double-counts a correction already made.

Direction is conservative - it costs power rather than manufacturing false positives
(critical value inflated 2.2% at n=300/AR(1) up to 13.4% at n=120/AR(2); a true |t|
of 3.5 is reported as p=0.00086 instead of 0.00058). But the quantity is arbitrary,
and the package contains a correct phi-aware implementation used by a DIFFERENT path
(.compute_ar_effective_df_compat, R/fmriAR_adapter.R:579).

Also: method="satterthwaite" is a literal no-op alias - R/effective_df.R:51-57
duplicates :47-50 verbatim.

NOT a simple repair: the function never receives phi, so making it phi-aware is an
API change, and "correct" requires choosing a reference-distribution contract
(normal / Satterthwaite / calibrated-t). Interacts with variance work: this
conservative bias partially cancels the anti-conservative SE miscalibration under
AR misspecification, so the two must be fixed and validated together.

A change-detector test pinning current behaviour is already in
tests/testthat/test-variance-closed-form.R - fixing this will break it on purpose.
set.title: Bug: AR effective df is phi-blind and governs every AR p-value
